value.deck: A company called DeepSeek has released a new, free tool that helps computers write their own code, offering an alternative to existing paid options.
shortVersion: DeepSeek, an AI company, has launched a new tool called DeepSeek Harness. This tool helps computers write their own software code. It's "open-source," meaning its inner workings are freely available for anyone to see and use.

DeepSeek Harness is designed to compete with other popular AI coding tools, like Claude Code. Because it's open-source, developers can use it without paying and even change it to fit their needs. DeepSeek also released a more powerful version of its AI, called DeepSeek-V4-Pro, which is better at these coding tasks, but it costs more to use.
value.plainLanguage: DeepSeek has released a free, open-source tool that helps AI write computer code, giving developers a new choice over paid options, alongside a more powerful but pricier AI version.

keyTerms.meaning: Software that anyone can see, use, and change. Think of it like a recipe shared freely for everyone to cook with and improve.
Computers that can think and learn, similar to how people do, to solve problems or create things.
A set of tools and rules that make it easier for programmers to build software. It's like having a pre-built structure for a house that you can then customize.

A way for different computer programs to talk to each other and share information. Imagine a waiter taking your order (request) to the kitchen (another program) and bringing back your food (the result).

value.whyItMatters: This matters because having an open-source tool for AI coding means more people can use and improve it without high costs. It gives software developers a free, transparent choice instead of relying only on expensive, private tools, potentially speeding up how new software is created.
watchNext: See how many software developers start using DeepSeek Harness for their projects.
Observe if other companies also release their own free, open-source AI coding tools.
